ov: A lean, hardy wild dog of Australia, ginger, black-and-tan or creamy white. Its lineage split early from the one that led to today’s domestic dogs; the oldest dingo remains in Australia are about 3,500 years old.

why.dm: Dingoes live wild, but whether they count as a form of domestic dog, a wolf subspecies or their own species is still debated.

cf.tip: Dingoes come from an early branch of the dog family tree, split off before today’s domestic breeds.

fx: A dingo can run at up to 60 km/h.
notes: The existing fact is confirmed: dingoes can rotate their wrists to turn doorknobs and raise latches, and their flexible shoulders let them climb fences. The article says fences, not trees.
